prompt.brief: Design a safety-critical vehicle-perception stack that time-synchronizes camera, LiDAR, and radar data, detects and tracks 3D objects, estimates motion, and exposes confidence and sensor-health state to planning.
successSignals: Define sensor calibration/time sync, frame IDs, object tracks, classes, covariance/confidence, occlusion, free space, and safety contracts.
Bound compute and memory for deterministic latency; detect sensor degradation, out-of-distribution scenes, stale frames, and conflicting modalities.
Separate safety-critical online inference from dataset logging, labeling, training, replay, simulation, and model rollout validation.
Explain redundancy, fail-safe behavior, uncertainty propagation, privacy, hardware failure, observability, and minimum-risk degraded perception.

functional: Capture synchronized sensor frames, calibrate/fuse them, detect 3D objects/free space, track motion, and publish timestamped scene hypotheses.
Expose confidence, sensor health, track history, occlusions, latency, and uncertainty to planning/control with explicit safety limits.
Support model/configuration versioning, replay/simulation, secure fleet telemetry, rollback, sensor dropouts, and incident evidence capture.
nonFunctional: Meet deterministic end-to-end perception latency under 100ms with timestamp integrity and bounded behavior under sensor degradation.
Process 30 frames per second across a fleet while keeping training/replay workloads off the vehicle critical path.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 30 FPS sensor fusion per vehicle across a 100k-vehicle fleet
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Safety-critical vehicle-perception stack records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
